mi355x-dlc-rack.description: Basis: Supermicro L11 rack SRS-48ULC-MI355-4U8N-R0. It is a 48U 19-inch rack with 8x AS-4126GS-NMR-LCC 4U direct-to-chip liquid-cooled servers (8x MI355X 288 GB, 1400 W TBP, plus 2x EPYC 9005 each), giving 64 GPUs per rack. It also holds a 4U in-rack CDU (100 or 250 kW, supports up to 45 C facility water), a vertical manifold plus 8 horizontal manifolds, 2 data switches and 1 management switch. Each server has 4x 6600 W (2+2) Titanium PSUs on 200-240 VAC; there is no rack busbar or power shelf, so the PSU sets are modeled as 8 'shelves'. The 'ac_54v' input means AC-fed. Because the CDU is in the rack, the rack connects to facility water, not a hall CDU secondary loop. Cold plates cool the GPUs and CPUs; fans cool memory, NICs, drives and PSUs. The rack is useful as a mixed-hall type next to Helios or NVIDIA racks. Dell's alternative is the PowerEdge XE9785L: 3 OU nodes in an IR7000 21-inch rack with 33 kW power shelves.

Each server's PSUs are 2+2 redundant, so losing one feed leaves 16 PSUs = 105.6 kW for the servers; Supermicro's 120.36 kW rack power also covers the in-rack CDU and switches, assumed on separate PDU outlets. The rack-level shelf check (lose one shelf) does not capture per-server 2+2 limits.

rubin-ultra-kyber.description: Roadmap entry; most values are estimates. Kyber rotates compute blades vertically like books: GTC 2026 showed 2 chassis x 18 compute sleds, each with 4 Rubin Ultra GPU packages (4 reticle dies, 1 TB HBM4e each) and 2 Vera CPUs, i.e. 144 packages / 576 dies in one NVLink 7 domain. Rear NVLink switch blades plug into a passive midplane instead of cable cartridges. Power is 800 V DC only (NVIDIA: 54 V in-rack distribution hits physical limits above ~200 kW; it showed an 800 V sidecar powering 576 Rubin Ultra GPUs in one Kyber rack at GTC 2025): an adjacent power sidecar rectifies 415/480 V AC to 800 V DC; the APC sidecar shown at GTC 2026 held 7 x 3U 110 kW 800 V power shelves, 4 x 2U DC output PDUs, a 4U power management controller and 5 Li-ion battery backup units. The footprint here treats the compute rack plus its power sidecar as one placed unit (about two 600 mm slots). Cooling is all-liquid via the facility TCS through a CDU; NVIDIA has not published whether a cooling sidecar is used.

amd-helios-pod4.description: Four amd-helios racks (288 MI455X GPUs, 4 separate 72-GPU UALoE scale-up domains) in a row with one network-rack holding scale-out leaf switches. In 0.6 m slot units, each double-wide Helios takes 2 slots (offsets 0, 2, 4, 6) and the network rack sits at slot 8.
amd-helios-pod4.name: AMD Helios pod (4 racks + 2 network racks)
amd-helios-pod4.notes: The pod size is an assumption. AMD publishes no pod grouping for Helios: the scale-up domain is one rack, and racks join only over the Ethernet scale-out fabric. The Schneider/AMD reference design sizes clusters by MW (up to 10.4 MW), not by a fixed rack count. Four racks were chosen as a convenient row unit of about 1 MW (4 x 246 kW planning peak). Scale-out links are not listed here: the twin's network solver derives them from each rack's scale_out_ports (216 x 800G per Helios with 3 Vulcano NICs per GPU) and routes them. Two network racks are included because 864 leaf-facing 800G ports exceed one network rack: at 1:1 oversubscription a 144-port leaf has 72 downlinks, so 864 ports need 12 leaves, and the catalog network rack holds 8 switches (estimated). Front-end (18 Salina 400G DPUs per rack) and management links are not counted.

gb300-su8.description: DGX SuperPOD-style scalable unit (SU): 8 gb300-nvl72 racks (576 GPUs, eight separate 72-GPU NVLink domains) in one row with 2 network-rack members in the middle. In 0.6 m slot units, compute racks take one slot each (offsets 0-3 and 8-11) and each 800 mm network rack takes two slots (offsets 4 and 6), so all members are contiguous. NVIDIA's DGX GB300 SuperPOD RA gives ~1.2 MW TDP per SU.
gb300-su8.name: GB300 NVL72 scalable unit (8 racks + 2 network racks)
gb300-su8.notes: From NVIDIA's DGX SuperPOD RA for DGX GB300: each SU is 8 DGX GB300 NVL72 racks at ~1.2 MW TDP. The compute fabric is a rail-optimized, non-blocking fat tree on Quantum-X800 Q3400-RD (144 x 800G) switches, with 8 leaf switches per SU (4 rails x 2 leaves). Spines are added only beyond one SU (8 spines for 2 SUs, 36 for 8 SUs). The storage/in-band Ethernet fabric adds 4 SN5600 leaves per SU, plus SN2201 out-of-band switches and management/UFM nodes. The network-rack count is an estimate: NVIDIA's rack-layout figure is not in text form. Sizing: 8 racks x 72 ConnectX-8 800G ports = 576 compute-fabric ports. At 1:1, a 144-port leaf has 72 downlinks, so 576 / 72 = 8 leaves, which matches NVIDIA's count and fills one catalog network-rack (8 switches). A second network rack holds the 4 SN5600 Ethernet leaves, OOB and management gear, and room for spines when SUs are combined. Both network racks sit mid-row to shorten leaf cable runs. links is empty because each NVL72 is a self-contained NVLink domain: there is no inter-rack copper scale-up cabling. Scale-out links are derived by the network solver from each rack's scale_out_ports. Some OEM SU layouts differ: Gigabyte's GB300 GIGAPOD uses 16 compute + 8 management racks per SU.
